prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B003 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested it from several directions and the scientific case held. The discovery arc is complete and bounded: Holst's human physiology of GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action, Drucker's proglucagon, receptor and intestinotropic biology, and Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active 7-36 form. It is followed by replicated randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Maturity is not in doubt. The chair's first question, whether the citation should rest on physiology or on the therapy, is answered most defensibly by physiology and the active peptide, with the incretin therapies named as the consequence. That framing is the one in which the three names form a coherent set, and it is the framing the committee can state openly if it is asked why the long-acting analogue programme is not credited.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem has not been resolved by the discussion, only clarified. Every member, including me, relies on the same recalled and unverified account of the priority for the active peptide, and Habener and other early peptide investigators remain outside the credited list. Excluding Knudsen is a judgement that discovery outranks engineering, and El Manira is right that if the citation were framed around the therapy her claim would be at least as strong as Mojsov's. A prize that honours only the antecedents of a drug class that reaches patients through industrial analogues can look incomplete, and the unanimity across six members raises a risk of choosing the safe candidate over the cleanest allocation. I judge these costs acceptable for B003 but not trivial.

responses.point: She would accept Knudsen only if Mojsov is dropped, and she proposes June and Sadelain alone for B018, treating Rosenberg as a forerunner distinct from CAR design.
responses.response: I considered the swap seriously and I do not make it. Replacing Mojsov with Knudsen would convert a discovery prize into a drug-development prize, and it would make the physiology narrative incomplete, because identification of the active 7-36 form is the discrete and testable step that links Holst's and Drucker's biology to pharmacology. On B018, my view from round 1 stands and I would add that the committee cannot cure the missing originator by trimming Rosenberg. Eshhar's absence is the same problem for a pair or a trio. Her point that the CAR construct and costimulation design are what is specific to the prize is fair, but it makes B018 a decision about the principle of credit, which we have not settled, and that is why it stays an alternative and not a second part.

responses.point: He states that Knudsen's claim is at least as strong as Mojsov's if the B003 citation is framed around therapy, and he sees a two-part prize involving B043 or B018 as conceivable but forcing a split of credit his evidence does not support.
responses.response: I agree with the conditional and it is why the framing matters: if the citation named the therapy, I would reopen the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen, and I would then have to ask whether Drucker and Holst are the right physiological anchors. I do not accept that framing, because the physiology and the active peptide are what the committee can credit without crediting an industrial programme. On two parts I agree with you. Because of the three-person cap, adding B043 or B018 would force one of the B003 names out, or would force a truncated allocation of the second part, and I see no combination in which both parts are fair. I note your disclosed closeness to circuit neuroscience, and I weigh optogenetics on the same terms as the others: mature and independently validated, but a method whose attribution is the least clean on the shortlist.

responses.point: He asks whether the prize should reward physiology, drug design or both, and proposes adding Ishikawa for cGAS-STING while ranking it fourth.
responses.response: My answer to his question is physiology and the active peptide, with the drug design cited as consequence, and I would write the committee statement so that the omission of the analogue programme is acknowledged. On B034 I still resist the third name for the reason I gave: Sun and Wu did the biochemical work in Chen's laboratory, so a Chen, Barber and Ishikawa trio leaves a line that is difficult to defend. I agree with his own maturity caveat. A secure mechanism without clinical validation is a legitimate future candidate but I would not put it ahead of a field whose benefit is already measured in randomized trials.

responses.point: The chair holds that the objection to B045 on grounds of indirect medical relevance is weaker than it first appears, and that the roles of Ron, Harding and Kaufman on PERK and ATF6 stay open.
responses.response: I accept that Mori and Walter are the cleanest two-person attribution on the list, and that the indirect relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer is real, so I do not dismiss B045 on those grounds. I keep it outside my alternatives because the chair's own caveat about Ron, Harding and Kaufman means the allocation is less closed than it looks, and because the disease link is mostly mechanistic and not yet an outcome. I also take from his summary that the unresolved priority evidence on the active GLP-1 peptide is shared by all of us. I would ask that the committee record that it was treated as a stated uncertainty and not as a settled fact.

uncertainties: The priority evidence for the active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov relative to Habener and other early investigators) cannot be settled from the supplied record, and the trio rests on a judgement that I cannot independently verify.
Whether the committee will accept a physiology-and-active-peptide citation when the benefit reaches patients through analogues designed in industry, and how the omission of Knudsen is acknowledged.
For B018 and B043, whether any defensible three-name allocation exists given Eshhar's absence and six optogenetics names, which is why they remain alternatives only.
statement.conflict_note: No update to my round-1 disclosure. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share an institution with other members; none of these ties involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and shared affiliation is not in itself a conflict. I request no recusal.
